The token needs to be carefully distributed to stakeholders based on the impact and ecosystem development, as an alternative to investor funding.
A rewards system needs to be designed to redistribute tokens/wealth and participation as the incentive, which drives more impact and stakeholder ownership.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem uses a token-based economic model to incentivize and reward stakeholders for their participation in regenerative agriculture and sustainable food systems.

The Fresh Earth Token (FET) is a verifiable science and technology-based token that measures the impact of regenerative practices using key performance indicators (KPIs) such as carbon sequestration, biodiversity, water retention, reduction in chemical use, and increase in food quality.
The Fresh Earth Token is unique to each country and represents fractional ownership of a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) that manages the food ecosystem business.

The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes an expert community, which is an autonomous decentralized and transparent community-governed ecosystem with open sourced and independently verifiable measures of impact.

The retail marketplace is a four-sided ecommerce platform that connects Consumers with Farmers, Designers (programs), and Manufacturers (products) with supply chain (Packers, Drivers, Physical Stores).
The Consumer Movement, also known as the Consumer App, allows consumers to create their own food health and farming system by building the community and an accurate demand profile.
The Fresh Earth Impact Validation (FEIV) is a score related to a global standard of measurement against four KPIs: Health, Economy, Food Quality, and Environment.

The Fresh Earth Rewards (FER) system is designed to redistribute tokens and wealth among stakeholders based on their impact, participation, and ecosystem development, as an alternative to investor funding.
Transactions within the Fresh Earth platform are transparent, meaning that any user can understand the breakdown of what percentage each person in the process is making.

The key element of the transparent ledger is to keep the money within the ecosystem and encourage sharing of wealth between stakeholders and optimization of costs through participation and 'Data Comms' nudging.

The motivations behind the Crusades differed between the various classes of European society.
The nobility saw the Crusades as an opportunity to gain wealth, land, and prestige.
The Church saw the Crusades as an opportunity to spread Christianity and to defend the Holy Land.
The merchants saw the Crusades as an opportunity to gain access to new markets and to expand their trade networks.
The peasants were motivated by religious fervor and a desire to earn pardon for their sins.
Richard I was the King of England from 1189 to 1199.
Richard the Lionheart was a central figure in the Third Crusade.
Louis IX of France led the Seventh Crusade in 1248.
Saint Louis IX believed it was his duty to defend the Holy Land and to spread Christianity.
Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade in 1095.
Godfrey of Bouillon was a prominent French nobleman who participated in the First Crusade.
Godfrey became the first ruler of the Kingdom of Jerusalem after the capture of the city in 1099.
The peasants of medieval Europe believed that by participating in Crusades, they could atone for their sins and earn salvation.
The Church offered the promise of eternal reward to those who participated in the Crusades.
Jerusalem was seen as the holiest city in Christendom.
The peasants believed that God was on their side and that He would intervene in their favor.
For many peasants, participating in the Crusades offered them an escape from the monotony of their everyday lives.
The Crusades opened up trade routes to new markets in the Middle East and Asia.
The Crusaders had a significant naval fleet, which provided protection for European merchants traveling to the Holy Land.
Many European merchants were hesitant to engage in long-distance trade due to the dangers involved.
The Crusades created a demand for religiously significant goods, such as relics, Christian artifacts, and holy water.
The Crusades did contribute to the spread of diseases like the bubonic plague due to the large numbers of people traveling to and from the Holy Land.
People during the medieval period did not have the same understanding of medicine and disease that we do today.

Mycorrhizal fungi are found in many ecosystems besides forests, including grasslands, wetlands, deserts, and agricultural fields.
Most plant species form a symbiotic relationship with mycorrhizal fungi.
Mycorrhizal fungi are present in almost all soils.
Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi colonize the roots of over 80% of all plant species, including grasses, legumes, and most crop plants.
Ectomycorrhizal fungi are mainly associated with woody plants and form symbiotic associations with trees and shrubs such as oaks, pines, birches, and willows.
Different types of plants tend to form associations with different types of mycorrhizal fungi.
Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi form associations with a wide range of plant species including crop plants, grasses, and many other types of plants.
Ectomycorrhizal fungi form more specific associations with trees and shrubs, particularly with conifers like pines, firs, and spruces.
